issues.detail: The PBM equation is exact as a relation among t, v^2, tau_eff, and MSD, but the source does not give numerical branch-specific v^2 or tau_eff values, nor functions of the traction controls (F0,tau_V) or tension controls (Delta T,tau_T) that determine them. The long-time formula therefore cannot return raw MSD for either hidden activity mode. Treating v^2 and tau_eff as Player controls would change measured/fitted readouts into interventions and violate the source semantics.

The only closed normalization derivable from Eq. (MSD) removes v^2 and tau_eff and yields one universal curve shared by traction and tension fluctuations, so the two branch programs would be identical. The separate two-branch behavior mentioned later concerns MSRD corrected/scaled by T1 quantities, but the TeX supplies no branch equations, coefficients, point table, or common numeric response function. Thus neither route yields two distinct source-contained branches over one readout and one public control interface.

F0,tau_V,Delta T,tau_T are the manipulated activity parameters, but their numeric values and domains are absent from the frozen TeX. Moreover, traction and tension use different parameter pairs with different physical meanings and qualitatively different persistence effects; no source-defined common control maps one pair to the other. t*=2500 tau_R is a fixed evaluation time, while v^2,tau_eff,l_v and the displacement statistics are measured quantities, so none repairs the missing shared intervention domain.

The ScienceCard contains claims=[] and therefore no quantitative_form tied to a claim, no oracle_outputs AST, and no claim-specific domains, readouts, mechanisms, or private branch conditions that an eligible review could select. The mechanism-level PBM equation alone is not executable under the review contract. This accurately reflects the paper-level missing branch data and cannot be repaired by selecting the existing unreported controls.

The quantitative_form correctly quotes 1/xi=W^2 S(2k)/(8 sin^2 k), but oracle_outputs is labelled localization_length_xi and computes W^2/[(1/8)S(2k)]=8W^2. It both returns the inverse physical trend and omits sin^2(k). From epsilon_k=-2 cos k and E=-1.8, k=acos(0.9), sin^2(k)=0.19; with chi=0.1, k0=0.2*pi<2k so S(2k)=1. The source-leading output is therefore xi=1.52/W^2, not 8W^2. Direct checks give card/source-leading values 0.08/152 at W=0.1 and 0.0008/15200 at W=0.01. Rebuild the AST as the inverse of the complete source right-hand side and anchor every derived constant.

The source gives 1/xi=W^4 times the full k,k0-dependent bracket divided by 32*pi*sin^2(k). The card AST instead returns W^4/0.03125=32W^4 under the xi key. This reverses xi proportional to W^-4 into xi proportional to W^4. Moreover, 0.03125=1/32 is not the coefficient supported by either source equation: even the near-k0=pi leading prefactor begins with 1/(64*pi) and still multiplies (pi-k0)sec^2(k)/sin^2(k). At E=-1.8, chi=0.2, direct execution of the full source expression yields C=0.3063898164 in 1/xi=CW^4, hence xi=3.263816049/W^4; the card gives 0.0032 at W=0.1 instead of approximately 32638.16. Replace the parameter and AST with the complete anchored source relation.

The second claim treats chi=0.2,0.25,0.3 as one branch with one coefficient. The exact source expression depends on k0=2*pi*chi, so these are not interchangeable fixed contexts: evaluating Eq. (second-order) at E=-1.8 gives different inverse-xi coefficients approximately 0.30639, 0.11848, and 0.064013. The near-pi expansion is explicitly an expansion around chi=1/2 and cannot be substituted without a stated error for chi=0.2-0.3. Select exactly one source-reported second-order chi for the matched world and use the full expression for that k0, or encode separate claims; do not average or reuse one coefficient.

The frozen TeX states only W<<1 and says the figure plots xi versus log W; it does not enumerate the plotted W values. The ScienceCard nevertheless invents the continuous interval 0<=W<=1. W=0 is a singular xi query (the source equations give 1/xi=0 and thus xi diverges), and W=1 is not W<<1 when the hopping amplitude is set to unity. The asymptotic series also has a non-perturbative remainder, so no unstated exact cutoff may be inferred. A revised card needs a finite positive domain tied to exact frozen-source evidence. If numerical W values can only be read from an omitted figure, extend and re-freeze the source packet first; otherwise this paper cannot support the point-Oracle domain.

The scientific discriminator is chi: the first claim is chi=0.1 and the second is chi in {0.2,0.25,0.3}. Yet both claims cite only the same energy/system-size/averaging conditions, while stealthiness_chi is declared as a global public control but appears in neither claim.control_names nor either AST. Consequently there are no disjoint branch-specific fixed conditions that an eligible review can select, and exposing chi would add an ignored public intervention. Keep W as the shared public control; add source-anchored private conditions chi=0.1 and one definite second-order chi and cite exactly one from each claim. Keep E=-1.8 and the model definition common.

The ASTs purport to evaluate perturbative analytic leading-order laws, but both claims attach the finite-size L<=800000 and at-least-1000-realization/20-eigenstate protocol as fixed conditions, and the readout is described as the fractal-dimension-extracted numerical statistic. The source says the numerics confirm scaling; it does not provide pointwise numerical xi values, fitted amplitudes, or error bars that equal the analytic AST. Revise the selected readout explicitly as the deterministic leading perturbative localization-length prediction and keep the numerical protocol only as supporting statistical provenance, not as hidden physical branch conditions. Preserve source_unspecified for the unreported fit/error convention and do not present it as sampled per-query noise.

The S_2k_value=1 parameter is anchored only to the step-spectrum definition, which does not by itself establish its value at E=-1.8 and chi=0.1; the derivation additionally requires epsilon_k=-2cos k, k0=2*pi*chi, and the reported branch condition. The W control anchors omit the source definition w_q=W A(q)eta_q, variance W^2 S(q), and the hopping-unity convention needed for its dimensionless scale. The second-order parameter's locator does not support its numeric value at all. A revised card must give each executable parameter and unit the complete locator chain used to derive it.

The card says the second-order coefficient is merely an integral/not closed form and simultaneously sets case_authoring_ready=true with a symbolic coefficient. The frozen supplement actually evaluates the integral and gives an explicit trigonometric/logarithmic expression for 1/xi at 2k<k0<pi-k. What is missing is a correct machine encoding at one selected chi, not a source equation. Replace the vague quantitative_form and invented scalar by the full expression (or an exactly precomputed, fully located coefficient for one chi), then remove the resolved ambiguity only after source review. Until then the ready flag is premature and an eligible review would also be blocked by the ambiguity's links to the selected claim, mechanism, control, condition, and readout.

issues.detail: Eq. (6) is a valid symbolic relation, but the source gives no numeric r or lambda_0^2/mu and calls rho a non-universal number in the open interval (0,1). It also does not fix phi dot phi or the relevant Phi amplitudes. Therefore raw f_eff cannot be returned as an objective numeric value from q alone. Assigning value 1 to these quantities is an invented benchmark world, not a paper-grounded central value; rho=1 directly violates the stated interval.

The critical AST evaluates 0.5 q^2 and the gapped AST 1+0.5 q^2 after the placeholders are materialized. The second result simultaneously substitutes phi dot phi=1 and Phi_1=Phi_4=Phi_5=1, although the orthonormal decomposition implies those three unit amplitudes alone contribute 3 to phi dot phi. Moreover, the source distinguishes the Phi_1 coefficient (1-rho) from the Phi_4/Phi_5 coefficients 1. At q=0.5 the AST returns 1.125, whereas its own component assignments in Eq. (6) give 1.375; a pure Phi_4 state gives 0.625 and a pure Phi_1 state with the invalid rho=1 gives 0.125. Thus the executable output is not the quoted quantitative_form for a defined branch state.

The source states only that the construction concerns infinitesimal but nonzero momenta. The card invents the closed interval 0<=q<=1: the lower boundary violates q!=0 and the upper boundary has no stated scale, unit convention, or applicability guarantee. Representative execution at q=0,0.5,1 is therefore only execution of the card, not source-valid evidence. No exact finite point-query domain can be recovered from this frozen packet.

The two claims cite only the same common medium and classical-theory conditions; the card defines no private critical-direction versus gapped-direction condition that an eligible matched review could select. The gapped claim further pools Phi_1, Phi_4, and Phi_5 although Eq. (6) assigns Phi_1 the distinct coefficient 1-rho and the paper identifies different momentum directions for Phi_1 and Phi_4. This is not one well-defined hidden branch with one Oracle program.

Equations (Curv) are the ideal limiting Poisson and GUE distributions. For the actual BGATE histograms, the source says only that the data have general similarity to GUE, do not exhibit a perfectly flat small-k plateau, and reproduce the defining large-k exponents; the figure caption calls the polynomial fits consistent with exponents 4 and 2. The claim ASTs instead return the complete ideal curves as exact empirical probabilities for every k, including k=0. Revise the card to represent either the ideal theoretical laws or the source-reported empirical tail statistic, without changing one into the other.

The source leaves N_POI and N_GUE as normalization constants; it never sets either to 1. The AST therefore yields unnormalized densities. Conditional on the source's signed curvature definition and normalization over all real k, elementary integration gives N_POI=1/pi and N_GUE=2/pi; for a nonnegative magnitude density the constants would instead be 2/pi and 4/pi. At k=1 the card returns 0.5 and 0.25, whereas the signed normalized ideal densities would both be 1/(2*pi), approximately 0.1591549431. Because the histogram sign/folding convention is not stated in the frozen text, a revision should use an explicitly justified convention or a normalization-free shape ratio rather than an invented prefactor.

The source defines k from kappa_n=d^2 phi_n/dt^2, so k is signed; it does not define the card's control as a nonnegative magnitude. It also gives no finite [0,100] range. The empirical power-law statement applies only as |k| becomes large, making the lower boundary k=0 inapplicable, while k=100 is an arbitrary cap with no reported bin, fit range, or resolution. The exact AST values at those boundaries are thus card outputs, not source-backed BGATE evidence.

The source reports 30 equally spaced time segments, each 0.5 ns long, for a fast gate whose duration is 50 ns. It does not enumerate segment centers. The ScienceCard invents the contiguous midpoint list 0.25,0.75,...,14.75 ns and simultaneously says those points cover the gate duration; they span only the first 15 ns. Remove time_t if it is not part of the selected interface, or recover the actual segment locations from an expanded source packet.

The claimed discriminator is the very first time interval versus all other intervals, but both claims cite exactly the same bgate_fast, system_params, and hilbert_dim conditions. No disjoint initial-interval and noninitial-interval fixed conditions exist for the matched branch gate. Moreover, the later empirical histograms need not share one pointwise curve; the source supports only a common fitted tail exponent. A revised card must add source-anchored private conditions and bind only the statistic actually shared within each branch.

The card itself records curvature_normalization as an ambiguity linked to both selected claims, the mechanism, control, condition, and readout, yet sets case_authoring_ready=true and materializes the unknown constants as 1. source_unspecified correctly records missing source information; it does not license a central value. Resolve the readout semantics and normalization in a new card, or retain the ambiguity and reject drafting.

Both the human quantitative_form and the source say S_SS=2.94 log(t)+1.33 at fixed g^2=15, but claim.control_names and oracle_outputs use g2 inside log. The executable card therefore answers a different scientific question. At g2=1,5,15 it returns 1.33, 6.0617474626, and 9.2916675912, values that correspond only to inserting t=1,5,15 into the time fit. Replace the public control with time t and make g^2=15 a source-anchored common fixed condition.

The source qualitatively reports approximately logarithmic-in-time SS growth across almost all g^2 curves in [0,15], but the numeric slope 2.94(2) and intercept 1.33(3) are explicitly the fit of the g^2=15 curve only. The current claim applicability and g2 control domain imply that one coefficient pair predicts entropy throughout the coupling interval, which the source never states. Preserve the broader coupling observation as provenance, but bind the executable coefficients only to fixed g^2=15.

Because the AST computes log(g2), the declared g2=0 boundary raises an undefined-expression error. After correcting the control to t, t=0 is likewise outside the logarithmic fit and cannot be used: the source separately states that the SS matrix-product initial state has bond dimension chi=4 and starts at entropy log_2(chi), whereas the fit would be singular. The TeX packet reports no fit-time endpoints or sampled time grid. Extend the source packet with the plotted/fitted positive time range before any deterministic point queries; do not invent bounds from the formula.

The card contains only one SS claim, so there are no disjoint source-contained branches and an eligible review cannot select a non-degenerate matched pair. The frozen supplement supplies the natural companion under the same m=1, g^2=15 and entropy protocol: S_GI(t)=0.386(6)t+0.43(2) versus S_SS(t)=2.94(2)log(t)+1.33(3). A new card should encode both relations, add GI and SS initial-state fixed conditions as mutually exclusive private conditions, and retain apparatus/model conditions as common.

The ScienceCard says it is unknown whether SS entropy is time-averaged. The supplement explicitly defines the time-averaged entropy with Delta t=2.5 and the Fig. S5 caption describes both GI and SS panels as time-averaged, while reporting both fits. Select this common statistic, add Delta t=2.5 as a common fixed condition, and remove the linked ambiguity only in a freshly reviewed card. Do not describe the Oracle as raw entropy if the selected fit comes from this averaged comparison.

All current fixed conditions belong to the SS claim and no GI condition exists. For the source-supported pair, N=8/PBC, m=1, g^2=15, the hardcore-gluon model, half-chain entropy definition, and Delta t=2.5 averaging are common; the equal superposition of superselection sectors and the gauge-invariant initial state are private alternatives. Encode this partition explicitly and ensure each claim cites only its own private condition plus every common condition.

issues.detail: The source gives the symbolic relation S^alpha(0,t)+C_alpha proportional to t^(-1/z) and says A_alpha, C_alpha, and z are fitted, but it does not report numerical amplitudes or offsets for either mode. The ScienceCard nevertheless assigns A_heat=A_sound=1 and C_heat=C_sound=0. Executing either AST therefore returns t^(-2/3), an invented normalized curve rather than an objective source-grounded correlation. The later source only establishes C_alpha proportional to 1/L, not its coefficient or the required mode-specific values.

The optimized_exponents claim states z_heat=1.52 and z_sound=1.51, exactly as the paper reports, but its sole oracle output is the parameter z_KPZ_exponent=1.5. Thus the executable truth returns 1.5 and cannot represent either fitted central value, much less distinguish the two branches. The theoretical 3/2 result and the two numerical estimates are different quantities and must not share one parameter.

The only numerical heat/sound values in the prose are global fitted exponents at the main parameter setting. The sound-velocity study states only that fitted exponents remain close to 1.5 and provides tested c_s values in a figure caption; it supplies no numerical z(c_s) values in the TeX. The time-dependent readout is not numerically closed because A_alpha and C_alpha are missing. Therefore neither time nor sound velocity supports an objective multi-point control-to-readout Oracle for two source-contained branches.

The source states the fitting range with strict inequalities, 40 < t < 4000. The card encodes minimum=40 and maximum=4000 as an ordinary continuous interval and therefore cannot establish that endpoint queries are valid. It also treats c_s={0,0.05,0.1,0.15} as a public response control although the source reports only qualitative robustness at those settings, not exact readout values.

Heat (alpha=0) and sound (alpha=plus/minus) are distinct modes in the source, but both proposed temporal-decay claims cite only the same three common fixed conditions. The card defines no heat-mode versus sound-mode branch condition, so it cannot select two disjoint hidden worlds under the benchmark's matched-family contract. This is structural in the current card and compounds the missing numeric curves.

Multiple selected locators are false against the frozen source: simulation_units_and_discretization cites 613-614, observation_protocol cites 621-626, the S_alpha averaging anchor cites 630-632, and the sound-velocity values cite line 805. Those ranges contain TikZ drawing definitions or a thermalization discussion. The corresponding scientific statements are found at 1613-1641 and 1802-1806. Since the reviewer must audit the frozen packet by line, these locators fail provenance even where the prose statement itself is recoverable elsewhere.

The statement that error bars are comparable to symbol size belongs to Fig. emfig3, which plots z versus c_s. The card transfers it to the S_alpha_correlation readout and both temporal-decay claims, although the cited temporal-correlation text does not state that uncertainty. The numerical fitted exponents also lack a specified uncertainty convention or numerical interval, as the card's own source_ambiguity acknowledges.

issues.detail: The AST simplifies to p^0.178 log(1+sqrt(2))/4. Direct execution returns W=0.0 at p=0, 0.162059614139479 at p=0.178, and 0.19476759467972907 at p=0.5. The source instead defines W as a normalized sum over loop configurations with a path-crossing sign and Boltzmann weight exp(-4 mu |h|); it never reduces that partition sum to the card's power law. The AST consequently supplies invented evidence rather than a source-reported central-value response.

The source states mu_c=(1/4)log(1+sqrt(2)), numerically 0.22034339675488573. The ScienceCard stores mu_c=0.44068679350977147, which is twice the anchored value. The rounded p_c^(2)=0.178 is source-reported, but it does not validate the incorrect mu_c parameter.

The paper gives the exact formal partition-sum definition and states only that the open string decays exponentially with endpoint distance in the topological phase and approaches a nonzero long-distance value after condensation. It provides no finite lattice, path geometry or length, closed partition function, tabulated values, fit coefficients, or saturation amplitude. Therefore a query containing only error_rate_p cannot objectively determine the claimed numeric readout.

The p=0 and p=1/2 anchors are explicit limiting settings used for the TEE calculation, while p_c^(2)=0.178 locates a transition. These three facts do not supply a pointwise open-string response over every p in [0,0.5]. Even if the physical channel can be tuned continuously, the selected readout remains numerically unclosed throughout that interval.

The card contains one claim and one bit-flip condition, so it cannot meet the required two disjoint branch claim sets and two private fixed-condition sets. The source says Pauli-Y and Pauli-Z errors can condense other paired anyons at the same threshold and that multiple condensates change the TEE, but it does not specify a second matched one-parameter channel, common p semantics, or a pointwise open-string/TEE response program for simultaneous error types. Turning those phase-classification statements into a second Oracle branch would add an unstated experimental parametrization.

The main-text density-matrix expression and supplementary doubled-space loop expression are two equivalent representations of the same normalized open-string expectation, not competing definitions. Recording them as an unresolved ambiguity is inaccurate, although removing that entry would not repair the missing numeric closure or matched branch.

issues.detail: The source equation is C(gamma,x)=c(gamma,L) x ln(x)+b(gamma,L) x, with c and b obtained separately by fitting for each gamma and fit-window upper size L. The card AST instead uses L in place of x and fixes both fitted coefficients to 1, so it evaluates C=L ln(L)+L and has no dependence on gamma. Direct evaluation gives 24.635532333438686 at L=8 and 132.03592144986465 at L=30 for all gamma. No such curve or coefficient assignment is reported.

The frozen source supplies neither numeric c(gamma,L) and b(gamma,L) tables nor closed functions for them. Its finite-size-scaling expression contains an unspecified scaling function f. The quoted zeta, nu, and gamma_c determine scaling variables and critical behavior, not the amplitude C at a requested control point. Therefore the selected controls cannot objectively determine a central-value C response.

In the source, x is the size coordinate varied within [8,L], while L labels the upper end of each fit window and reaches 30. The card removes x, exposes L as the sole size argument, assigns it the interval [8,30], and calls this integer linear lattice size continuous. Its gamma interval [0.1,0.4] is also unsupported as a closed response domain: the paper states a point at 0.1J and area-law behavior for gamma>=0.4J, not that 0.4J is a maximum. These domain choices would admit queries for which the paper gives no defined pointwise output.

The card stores c_log_coefficient=1 and b_area_coefficient=1 while its own roles acknowledge that both are fit-derived functions rather than fixed constants. Line 241 gives only their symbolic roles; it does not anchor either value to 1. The additional V_coupling_prefactor=1 record is an unnecessary algebraic placeholder rather than a reported fitted parameter. These records cannot be used as source truth.

The ScienceCard contains one claim and no two disjoint branch-specific condition sets. The logarithmic-law point at gamma=0.1J and area-law regime for gamma>=0.4J are outcomes along the same proposed public gamma control, not two hidden mechanisms or conditions with the same public controls and readout. The source does not provide a second pointwise numeric law under a distinct private condition, so Historical and alternate branches cannot share a valid Identification skeleton without adding an unstated world.

The source quotes plus/minus values for the FSS estimates but does not define their uncertainty convention. The card correctly records this as a source ambiguity attached to the selected claim, control, readout, mechanism, and fit condition. An eligible selection could not silently discard that unresolved provenance; in this case it is secondary to the missing executable response and branch pair.
